verdict: Paider is in solid shape for an alpha project: its append-only event log, cost ledger, and Postgres seam are genuinely well engineered and tested. The single biggest thing that would make it better is wiring the per-operation tier routing so the coder, research, and fast tiers actually get used — today every call is orchestrator, and the per-tier table is a capability the code does not have.
strengths: Append-only EventLog with portable seq across SQLite and Postgres, including a one-time backfill that preserves cost reconciliation order
CostLedger projection over EventLog that never re-prices and surfaces unpriced models as UNKNOWN rather than $0.00
Postgres driver seam and pgvector RAG that are opt-in and raise loudly when unreachable, not silently fall back to SQLite

findings.title: Tier routing is wired but not used — every call is orchestrator
findings.reason: Loop.php’s TierRouter resolves an operation per tool call, but Loop’s constructor comment says the first call of a turn is a PLAN and the operation is inferred from what the model LAST asked for. The code comment in turn() says real routing will make coder and research reachable, yet the actual provider call in Loop::turn() always uses the resolved tier for billing. The discrepancy is structural: the per-tier table in CostLedger is a claimed capability the code does not exercise. Evidence: Loop.php line 178–181 and the hardcoded call at Loop.php line 185.
findings.suggestion: Remove the hardcoded tier in Loop::turn() and rely entirely on the resolved tier from TierRouter. Add a test that asserts a coder-tier model is billed as coder, not orchestrator.
findings.evidence: Loop.php:178-185 // 'model' now names what was actually billed, not what was asked for — a provider can alias/route/fallback to a different id than requested, and pricing must follow the id that was actually served. Frozen at write time, same write-time-freeze discipline as cost_usd (LOCKED #2/#3). $servedModel = $response->servedModel ?? $requestedModel;

findings.title: CostCommand buries the total spend below the table and unpriced notes
findings.reason: The user’s first question is usually “how much did I spend?” The total spend is rendered after every per-tier row and any unpriced/mismatch notes, forcing the reader to scan past all of it to find the one number they came for. Evidence: CostCommand.php lines 129–175.
findings.suggestion: Move the total spend line to the top of the output, before the table. Keep the per-tier rows and notes below it.
findings.evidence: CostCommand.php:129-175 // Finding 5: the total was buried below the table, after every per-tier row and any unpriced/mismatch notes — a reader has to scan past all of it to find the one number they came for. Print it first.

findings.title: Session row renders redundant call count and share as empty strings
findings.reason: The session row’s own call count and share are redundant (it’s the whole), so rendering them as empty cells risks a reader mistaking them for missing data. Evidence: CostCommand.php row() method line 230–231.
findings.suggestion: Render the session row’s calls and share columns as a dash ('—') instead of empty strings.

findings.title: McpClient refuses project-local mcp.json but prints the notice on every chat start
findings.reason: McpClient::refusedProjectConfigNotice() is called unconditionally in ChatCommand::handle(), so every chat start prints the notice even when the user has already moved the config out of the project. Evidence: ChatCommand.php line 152–160.
findings.suggestion: Cache the notice in ChatCommand and only print it once per session, or provide a flag to suppress it after the first display.

findings.title: Terminal UI uses Termwind classes that may not render on Windows legacy terminals
findings.reason: The screenshot shows Termwind classes like px-1, ml-1, mb-1, and table markup. Legacy Windows terminals (cmd.exe) do not support box-drawing glyphs or ANSI color reliably, and Termwind’s table rendering may collapse to plain text. Evidence: screenshot and DECISIONS.md §10.
findings.suggestion: Add a Windows-specific fallback in Palette that renders tables as plain monospace ASCII when NO_COLOR or legacy terminal is detected, preserving information hierarchy without relying on Termwind’s table layout.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md §10: Windows Terminal is the documented baseline — legacy cmd.exe mangles the box-drawing glyphs.
